Actually size(obj) where obj is a frozenset of cells, so len = number of cells.

Hmm wait, size(x0) where x0 is objects set... order(x0, size) sorts each object by size (cell count). Then apply color. So each object becomes a color. So if a color forms multiple objects, it appears multiple times!

Let me re-check. objects returns set of objects (connected components). Each object is a single connected component of same color. So a color split into multiple components gives multiple entries.

In example: color 7 in input: 3x3-ish shape. Let's check connectivity: cells (0,0),(0,1),(0,2),(1,0),(1,1),(1,2),(1,3),(2,0),(2,1),(2,3),(3,3). Diagonal connected - yes all connected. (7,2),(7,3),(7,4),(8,2),(8,3),(9,2),(10,2),(10,3),(10,4) = 9 cells, 9 has 5 cells. So order 7,3,9 by size descending. Good.

For item 2: now components matter. Let me check each color's connectivity with diagonal=True.

Color 1: (3,5),(3,6),(3,7),(4,5),(5,5). All connected (3,5)-(3,6)-(3,7), (4,5) diagonal to (3,6) yes i-neighbor. (5,5) adjacent to (4,5). One object, 5 cells.

Color 2: (4,9),(4,10),(5,9). Connected diagonally: (4,9)-(4,10) adjacent, (5,9) adjacent to (4,9). One object, 3 cells.

Color 9: (7,0),(7,1),(7,2),(7,3),(8,0),(8,1),(8,2),(9,0),(9,2),(9,3),(9,4),(10,0),(11,0),(11,1). Is this one connected component? Let's check. (7,0..3) connected. (8,0),(8,1),(8,2) below. So 3 objects with sizes 14,5,3. Order: 9, 1, 2. Output [[9],[1],[2]].

Let me count explicitly: color 9: row7: 4, row8: 3, row9: 4, row10: 1, row11: 2 = 14. Yes.

So output 3x1: [[9],[1],[2]].

Then canvas each to 1x1, merge gives column [[2],[1],[9]]. Then hmirror reverses to [[9],[1],[2]]. Yes ascending sorted then reversed = descending. Confirms output [[9],[1],[2]].

Submit.
